claims.text: Restricting noble-metal precursor mobility during low-temperature reduction promotes stochastic atomic incorporation and favors single-phase high-entropy alloy nanoparticle formation.
The starting material is a uniform mixture of noble-metal single-source precursors.
The precursor metals can specifically be Pt, Ir, Os, Rh, and Ru.
The mixed precursors may be in either a solid or solution state.
The relevant synthesis regime is low-temperature reduction of mixed noble-metal single-source precursors.
Mobility-restricted synthesis causes nanoparticle lattice strain and defect incorporation.
Stochastic mixing under limited diffusion rates produces the proposed lattice strain and defects.
Limited atomic mobility reduces the opportunity for phase segregation between consecutive reduction steps.
Spatial confinement promotes random statistical incorporation of different metals.
A homogeneous single-phase high-entropy alloy can form even when its constituent elements reduce consecutively.
Mobility-restricted conditions will produce nanoparticles with uniform elemental mixing and a single solid-solution phase.
Conditions allowing greater precursor mobility will produce more phase separation or elemental segregation than mobility-restricted conditions.
Standard low-temperature reduction conditions naturally restrict atomic diffusion of noble-metal precursors.
The hypothesis applies to noble-metal high-entropy alloys synthesized at low temperature by reducing mixed single-source precursors.
The mechanism may not apply to high-temperature shock methods or element systems with radically different reduction kinetics.
The mobility-restriction threshold and kinetics required for optimal alloying are undetermined and may be material-specific.
In situ X-ray diffraction and multi-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy can track phase development, oxidation states, and local environments during reduction.
Formation of a comparably homogeneous single-phase alloy under increased-mobility conditions would falsify the proposed mobility-limitation mechanism.

contradictions.description: The baseline is defined as standard low-temperature conditions that already restrict diffusion, whereas the nominal control is deliberately adjusted to permit greater mobility. Thus the control is not the stated unchanged baseline, and the intervention-versus-baseline comparison is ambiguous.
